text:
katie-support: Hey team — PayRollCo just escalated: lots of 429s for their payroll-run endpoint this morning. They say overall TPS is only ~150 but they see sharp ~10s bursts of 429s. Can we triage?

devon: grabbing the request IDs they sent, sending logs now. Do we have their customer plan/rate-limits?

katie-support: They’re on paid standard tier, default quota last I checked: 1000 RPM, 300 TPS burst window. But they claim spikes are localized to a single region (us-west2).

samir-sre: pinging infra — checking gateway logs + edge rate-limiter counters. Quick thought: could be downstream proxy dropping connections and causing client retries to pile up.

rate-limit-bot: Summary (last 10m) for customer=payrollco: 429s=1.3k, 200s=28k, upstream-5xx=12, avg-latency=210ms, peak-rps=320.

ashok-eng: do we have specific x-rate-limit headers in customer traces? That will show whether it’s token-bucket exhaustion vs custom route cap.

devon: pasted sample response header from customer: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: r-12ab34
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 30
Retry-After: 1
```

devon: So headers indicate we hit global limit. But their client logs show short repeating retries every 200ms which could cause local storming.

julie-oncall: steps I’m taking: 1) enable debug logs for mgw in us-west2 for that customer (done), 2) create temporary soft increase for that customer to 1500 RPM for the next 30m, 3) advise customer to add jitter/backoff. Will report back in 10m.

katie-support: thx. I’ve already asked them to halt auto-retries for the payroll window and confirm backoff + jitter. They said their retry loop is built into the third-party SDK.

samir-sre: Logs show short-lived token-bucket full events on the Edge: repeated Acquire failures for customer token bucket id=cust-9876 between 08:09:22–08:09:38. Rate limiter applied local burst refill logic with window=1s. We need to examine burst-size vs refill rate.

devon: Are we sure it’s not a misrouted flood to a single gateway instance? I see one instance with CPU at 95% and others normal. Could be uneven hashing.

samir-sre: good call — checking consistent-hash distribution for customer route. Also checking nginx upstream 502 spikes that might trigger client retries.

rate-limit-bot: Notice: instance mgw-12 in us-west2 reported high accept-rate and repeated 429s, instance_load=0.94, redis-latency=7ms.

ashok-eng: If hashing is skewed we can flip to round-robin temporarily or add more partitions for that customer to spread tokens. But quick fix = increase per-customer quota, and tweak token-bucket burst-size to allow short spikes.

devon: Customer shared a curl repro. Putting it here for record: 

```bash
for i in {1..400}; do curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/payroll/run -d '{}' &
done
wait
```

katie-support: They ran this as part of a batched worker that accidentally parallelized. That explains concurrent short bursts.

julie-oncall: I’ve applied a temporary +50% RPM to cust-9876 and set auto-fallback policy to route to dedicated-slo pool if edge 429 rate > 10% for 2 minutes. Also scaled mgw in us-west2 by +2 pods.

payroll-ops: Confirmed we saw 429s drop to near-zero after scaling. Thank you. Concern: their payroll job is on a schedule — they might rerun if any failure occurs, so need to prevent retry-loop amplification.

samir-sre: action items from infra side: 
- investigate hashing/partitioning for route cust-9876 (likely hot-spot)
- consider adaptive per-customer burst window config (short-term 5s burst allowance)
- validate redis token-bucket fairness under high concurrency

ashok-eng: product/limits side: 
- add clearer headers: X-RateLimit-Burst, X-RateLimit-Window to help clients debug
- update docs on recommended exponential backoff + jitter examples for common SDKs

devon: sent customer guidance snippet for retries: 

```
Retry-After and jittered backoff recommended: 
base=0.5s
for n in 0..5: sleep = base * 2^n + random(0,0.5)
max attempts = 6
If you see X-RateLimit-Remaining=0 prefer queueing work and not immediate retry.
```

katie-support: Customer will patch SDK and run targeted single-threaded job for the next payroll-run. They also requested post-incident summary and quota increase request form.

julie-oncall: Logging notes: attach request IDs r-12ab34, r-12ab56 and timeframe 08:09:00–08:12:00 to postmortem. I’ll collect and add to incident board.

samir-sre: Follow-up: found a bug where the per-customer partition key used "account_id" but some of their requests used legacy "acct_id" — resulted in uneven sharding. Fix deployed to staging, rolling to prod in 10m. That likely contributed to hotspot.

devon: nice catch. That explains single-instance saturation.

katie-support: Final customer note: they want an SLA exception for this payroll window and proactive guidance for scheduled high-concurrency jobs. I sent the quota increase request to billing.

ashok-eng: Long term items: SDKs should expose built-in token bucket client-side counters and backoff helpers. Also we should update docs with safe defaults (max parallelism per account default = 50 for heavy endpoints).

julie-oncall: Incident resolved for now. I’ll create a short post-incident summary and assign owners for the infra + SDK changes.

payroll-ops: Thanks all — will confirm once SDK updated and next payroll run passes. :thumbsup:
